newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi-owned United Industrial votes to liquidate.
newsitem.headline: Saudi-owned United Industrial votes to liquidate.

text.p: Shareholders of Bahrain-based United Industrial Investment Co (UIIC) have voted to liquidate the company and close its Bahrain office, the company said.

"UIIC announces that its shareholders have agreed at an extraordinary meeting...to voluntarily liquidate the company and appoint the law office of (former Saudi oil minister) Sheikh Ahmed Zaki Yamani a liquidator," a UIIC announcement said.

UIIC, set up by Saudi investors in 1993, said shareholders agreed on February 24 to voluntarily liquidate the company, but did not say why. It asked creditors to submit their claims within a month to the liquidator.
Industry sources had earlier said the company had been planning to build a one million tonnes a year iron plant at a cost of $300 million to meet growing demand in the region.
They said UIIC had been negotiating with German engineering and contracting firms Mannesmann-Demag and Lurgi, a unit of Metallegesellschaft AG to build the iron plant in Bahrain.
